lines: MK04: Lead scoring, lifecycle and data hygiene [one-time]

sections: Our approach
We would deliver this with Marketo Engage.
What we would do
We will run a data audit, build the program that standardizes incoming data, and model lead scoring and the lead lifecycle with marketing and sales, through to the MQL handoff.

We will complete the initial setup steps and protocols, set up SPF and DKIM, the CNAMEs for branded tracking links and landing pages, install the Munchkin code on the website, and set up users and roles.

We will agree the field mapping with the CRM admin before the first sync, connect Marketo Engage to Salesforce or Dynamics, choose which fields sync or stay hidden, and check that the sync is running correctly.
We will design the program templates the team will clone (webinar, nurture, newsletter, event), with My Tokens, and build the branded email templates, landing pages and forms in Design Studio.

lines: O01: Monthly prompt and performance review [monthly]
O02: Content improvements for search and AI [monthly]
SI06: Monthly releases, monitoring and logs [monthly]
sections: Our approach
After launch, across the Adobe products in this proposal, our ongoing services for Brand Visibility, AEM Sites, Customer Journey Analytics and Brand Concierge are these.
After launch

We will maintain the prompt portfolio (200 to 1,000 prompts in up to three markets or languages) and three competitors; review up to five prompt changes, read the Impact Measurement Engine's results when Adobe generates an analysis for an eligible deployment pilot, prioritize up to 10 actions, and hold one review with you using five business measures.

We will refresh four existing pages and create one new answer/knowledge page using approved facts and existing templates, in one locale with two review rounds. Each page change is logged once and tagged search, AI or both.
Each month we will ship code through Cloud Manager pipelines, check the automatic AEM version updates, review logs and the Developer Console, and fix issues found after go-live.

lines: TC04: CJA audiences for Target, through Real-Time CDP or Journey Optimizer [one-time]
C06: Audiences that act on the data [one-time]
TC01: Target reporting setup in CJA [one-time]
sections: Our approach

A Target activity that uses CJA as its reporting source sends its data to Experience Platform (Web SDK is the preferred method), Adobe creates the Adobe Target Classification Events lookup dataset, and activity reports are built in CJA.

Supported Target activities report in CJA with its full journey data; Auto-Target and Automated Personalization do not. With Real-Time CDP or Journey Optimizer, audiences built in CJA reach Target too.
What we would do

We will build journey audiences in CJA, publish them to Experience Platform, and share them with Target through the Adobe Target destination, which needs Real-Time CDP or Journey Optimizer and a Target-enabled datastream, for the agreed personalization activities.

We will define up to five audiences from AI-referred visits and their outcomes in the CJA data view, publish them to Real-Time Customer Profile, and agree with you how each audience is used in its existing channels.

We will add the event dataset and the Adobe Target Classification Events lookup dataset (created by Adobe) to a CJA connection, then add activity and experience dimensions with persistence and the Experimentation context labels. Before each launch, confirm the activity type is supported and its reporting source is CJA with the agreed data view, since it can't change once live.
We will build Experimentation panel reports and a reusable Workspace template for Target activities, showing lift and confidence on your CJA success metrics.
